title: Owlkei Go Lifecycle State Machines
purpose: Document exact state transitions for app, requests, and connections

application_lifecycle.source: internal/core/app.go (New, Create), internal/core/container.go (wire), internal/core/options.go (AppOptions, checked at New), internal/core/server.go (Listen, Serve, Stop); user contract in internal/core/README.md

transitions.action: app := owlkei.New(opts) (nil = defaults)
effects: own HTTP router, container, memorybroker, built-in logger (log.NewLog(nil)), context pools
Publisher registered in the container
built-in HTTP and WS exception filters bound
trace.Tracer zero value (no listener)
AppOptions read once, copied and checked (panics 'invalid app: <Group>.<Field> …'); TLS files loaded
pre-route stages compiled in the fixed order loadshed, proxy, hostcheck, httpsredirect, headers, cors, csrf, compress (only those configured)
body cap AppOptions.HTTP.MaxBodyBytes (default 10 MiB)

transitions.action: binding code: BindGlobalMiddlewares, BindGlobalGuards, BindGlobalInterceptors, BindGlobalExceptionFilters (configuration is in AppOptions)
effects: each returns *App
after Create each panics 'invalid app: <Method> must be called before Create'
global middlewares run after the pre-route stages, whatever the bind order

transitions.action: app.Create(module)
order: container.wire(root): addGlobals(root), scanGlobals, discover (sync-set module factories called in dependency order on helper goroutines within the startup timeout; arguments from siblings, globals, Logger, Publisher), module states and needs, then per ready module in init order OnInit() and provide() of its providers, injectController for every controller of a ready module, probe and gate the controllers of pending modules
startAsync: one goroutine per AsyncImports entry
effects: every provider constructed once per app
all routes, events and layers registered
panics: 'invalid module: Create needs a root module', 'invalid app: Create called twice', 'dependency injection: ...', 'route conflict: ...', 'event conflict: ...'
module factory failures in Imports panic 'invalid module: module factory ...' (error, panic, nil module, startup timeout)
AsyncImports entries never stop Create; modules that need them stay pending

transitions.action: app.Listen() / app.Serve(listener) (port, TLS and h2c from AppOptions.Server)
effects: errors returned before binding: 'owlkei: Create must be called before serving', 'owlkei: app is already serving', 'owlkei: app is stopped', 'owlkei: listen on :<port>: <err>' (TLS / IsH2C conflicts panic at New)
startup log: InstanceLoader, RouteExplorer, WebSocketEvent, ServerListening
the call blocks until the server stopped

transitions.action: SIGINT / SIGTERM or app.Stop()
effects: AsyncImports ctx canceled first: no module changes state, no gate opens
signals no longer intercepted
listener and idle connections closed
running requests drained for ServerOptions.ShutdownTimeout (default 30 s), then their connections closed
waits for the AsyncImports goroutines until ShutdownTimeout since shutdown began; ModuleShutdownTimeout for each one abandoned
runShutdownHooks once per app (app.shutdownOnce): OnShutdown of ready modules only, in the reverse of the order they became ready; a panicking hook is logged as OnShutdownPanic and the others run
access log stopped after the hooks, suppressed panic stacks reported, stdout log pipeline flushed (at most 2 s) and synchronous again
returns nil, 'owlkei: shutdown timed out after <timeout>' or 'owlkei: serve: <err>'
WebSocket connections are not drained

transitions.action: app.Stop() on an app that is not serving
effects: OnShutdown hooks run once
later serving calls return 'owlkei: app is stopped'; ServeHTTP still answers

post_create_behavior: app.Create() can be called exactly ONCE (second call panics)
two apps in one process are independent (no package-level registry)

transitions.action: c := app.ctxPool.Get()
effects: Context object allocated or reused from pool

transitions.action: if r.Body is not nil / http.NoBody and the cap > 0: r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, cap); ctx.HTTPInit(c, &ex.writer, r)
effects: the cap is a plain int64 written once at New: 10 MiB, or AppOptions.HTTP.MaxBodyBytes (negative = off)
Request ID generated, X-Request-Id set
ResponseWriter/Request set

transitions.action: routing.Router.Match(method, path, version string, params []string) (*RouterItem, []string), retried with versioning.NeutralVersion on a miss
effects: the route's immutable httpRoute (layers, handler plan, filters)
the configured pre-route stages ran before the match; a stage that refuses answers itself, never 404 / 405 / 410 or the gate's 503
no route: global middlewares only, then 404 or 405 with Allow (precomputed bodies)

transitions.action: global middleware -> module middleware -> global guard -> module guard -> global pre-interceptor -> module pre-interceptor -> handler plan (pipes, then the handler) -> module post-interceptor -> global post-interceptor
effects: spec: .owlkei/request-pipeline.md section 1
a middleware without next(), a guard returning false (403 to the filters) or an interceptor without Pipe stops the chain
error in a middleware: the HTTP layer's fixed error response, no filter
error from a guard onwards: module filters (bound last first), global filters, built-in filter
with a tracer listener (only the access log): one event per stage and a complete event

transitions.action: write the result by kind, or the filter's response
effects: only exceptions reach the client with their code and message; any other panic answers a fixed 500 and is logged as UnhandledPanic
after a response was sent nothing more is written (ErrorAfterResponse logged)

transitions.action: app.releaseCtx(ex)
effects: ex.reset(): ctx.HTTPReset(c) clears all fields but keeps the capacity of the parameter values and the aggregation list (dropped over 64), the response writer points at nothing
Exchange returned to pool for reuse (not after an http.ErrAbortHandler re-panic)

http_request_lifecycle.panic_handling_location: HTTP.handleRequest() in internal/core/http.go: the request's only recover; middleware panics get the HTTP layer's error response, later ones the route's filters

context_mutation_rules.never_mutate_after: Guard stage (guard made decisions based on request state)

background_goroutines.dead_connection_detector: startDeadConnDetection (global, runs once at app.NewWS, interval 15s, timeout 60s)

transitions.action: HTTP Upgrade header received
effects: websocket.Handler called
Handshake function runs

transitions.action: Handshake middleware + guards pass
effects: websocket.Conn established
connID = handshake request ID (16 hex, from the trace scope)
Connection registered in WSConnMgr
LastSeen timestamp set

transitions.action: readLoop() spawned + writeLoop() spawned + pingLoop() spawned
effects: readLoop blocks on conn.Receive()
writeLoop blocks on send channel
pingLoop blocks on ticker (30s intervals)
sendChan := make(chan WSPayload, 32) created
done channel created for shutdown coordination
Client can send messages

transitions.action: Message received by readLoop (subscribe, publish, ping, pong, etc.)
effects: JSON unmarshaled to WSPayload
LastSeen timestamp updated
Topic pattern matching
Handler lookup
The layers (guard, interceptor, handler, filters); middlewares run only at the handshake
Handler can broker.Publish() for fanout

message_protocol.subscribe: Client → subscribe → Server sends ACK (empty message)
message_protocol.publish: Client → publish → Server dispatches event → Server sends ACK
message_protocol.ping: Server sends ping (30s) → Client responds with pong
message_protocol.pong: Client pong → Server records LastSeen (liveness check)

transitions.action: Client closes connection OR error in readLoop OR dead connection detected
effects: readLoop() exits
close(done) channel closes
pingLoop detects <-done close and exits
WSConnMgr.Unregister(connID) called
writeLoop() detects close on send channel and exits
All broker subscriptions cleaned up
Connection resources freed

dead_connection_detection.implementation: RWMutex: Read phase to collect dead IDs, Lock phase to cleanup one connection at a time

send_channel_semantics.overflow: message DROPPED silently if buffer full

context_lifecycle.per_message: new context for each incoming message

module_lifecycle_hooks.declaration: exported func() fields of core.Module, set on the built module (m.OnInit = func() {...})

timing.OnInit: during Create, when the module is initialized, before its providers are constructed
timing.OnReady: once per app at the end of Create, after routes, layers and the devtool snapshot exist; app.Get works inside it
timing.OnShutdown: once per app, on SIGINT/SIGTERM or app.Stop(), after running requests were drained

module_lifecycle_hooks.call_order: OnInit and OnReady run depth first, a module after the modules it imports (in Imports order, each once per app); OnShutdown runs in the exact reverse order. An app whose Create did not finish runs no OnShutdown.
module_lifecycle_hooks.panics: a panic in OnInit or OnReady stops Create unchanged; a panic in OnShutdown is logged (OnShutdownPanic) and the other hooks run

transitions.action: ModuleBuilder().Providers(MyProvider{})
provide(key): the providers its exported fields name first, then injectDependencies, then NewProvider()
effects: key: package path + type (genFieldKey)
constructed once per app, however many modules list it
an unresolvable field panics 'dependency injection: can't resolve dependency ...'
an unexported field panics 'dependency injection: can't set value to unexported ...'

transitions.action: the NewProvider result is set into controller, provider, layer and pipe fields
effects: injected by value: shared state sits behind a pointer

provider_lifecycle.critical_rule: NewProvider() is called once per provider type per app, at Create(); never call it yourself
provider_lifecycle.visibility: a module sees its own providers, those of the modules it imports, and the global ones (root module and IsGlobal modules)

module_initialization_order.critical: Create's call order is fixed (comment on App.Create in internal/core/app.go)
sequence: container.wire(root): addGlobals(root), scanGlobals, discover (sync-set module factories called in dependency order on helper goroutines within the startup timeout; arguments from siblings, globals, Logger, Publisher), module states and needs, then per ready module in init order OnInit() and provide() of its providers, injectController for every controller of a ready module, probe and gate the controllers of pending modules
startAsync: one goroutine per AsyncImports entry
dependencies: wire must run first: it fills the container everything else reads
initWS must run before the layer and handler init functions (they write WS state when WS is enabled)
initDevtool after routes and layers exist
callOnReady last; only then is the app marked created

module_states.source: internal/core/module_state.go, module_async.go, retry.go; design 0020; README.md › Module lifecycle

transitions.action: every AsyncImports entry the module needs is ready
effects: OnInit, providers, controllers (under wireMu)
gate opens in one atomic store
log ModuleReady
OnReady (a panic is logged OnReadyPanic, the module stays ready)

transitions.action: an entry it needs failed: factory error or panic, nil module, panic while building, type never resolved, controllers in an async factory's module, routes changed since the probe
effects: log ModuleFailed with the cause
its routes answer 503 without Retry-After forever
no OnShutdown

module_states.one_way: ready and failed never change again; after ready, run-time failures are the business code's job
module_states.need: M needs entry E when a provider of E's unit (or of a module that needs E) is the type of a field of M's providers, controllers, bound layers or pipes; importing alone is not a need

gate.http_pending: 503 ServiceUnavailableException body, Retry-After = seconds to the next Retry attempt (1-60) or 5
gate.layers: global middlewares run first; no module layer, filter or handler

module_states.retry: owlkei.Retry(ctx, *RetryOptions, fn): backoff InitialDelay 500 ms doubling to MaxDelay 30 s with jitter [d/2, d], MaxAttempts 0 = until ctx done; with an AsyncImports factory's ctx it reports attempts (ModuleRetry, devtool attempts / last_error, Retry-After)
